name: domain-health-check
description: Check a list of domains for email blacklist listings (Spamhaus DBL, URIBL, SURBL + IP-based ZEN/SpamCop/Barracuda) and missing email-auth DNS records (SPF, DKIM, DMARC). Use when the user pastes a list of domains — bare, one-per-line, comma-separated, or a CSV column — with no other instruction, or asks to check domains for blacklisting, blocklists, missing records, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, or email deliverability health. Pure public DNS, no API keys, no cost.
readme_snippet: Domain Health Check Checks every domain against 3 domain-reputation blacklists and 3 IP-reputation blacklists, plus SPF, DKIM (12 common selectors), and DMARC — using only public DNS. Requires Node 18+ on PATH (if node -v fails, tell the user Node 18+ is required and stop). Workflow Extract domains from whatever the user provided: bare list, comma/space separated, CSV column, URLs, or messy text. Take anything that looks like a domain. Don't ask for confirmation — just run. (The script itself also lowercases, strips https:///www./paths, dedupes, and skips invalid tokens.) Get the script: if a check.mjs file exists in the same directory as this SKILL.md, use it directly. Otherwise write the script below verbatim to a temp/scratchpad file named check.mjs. Do not modify it. Run it once for the whole batch: node check.mjs domain1.com domain2.com ... — it prints JSON. For very large lists (300+), split into runs of 250 and merge results. Expect roughly 10–30 s per 50 domains.

name: memory-recall
description: Search and recall relevant memories from past sessions via MemSearch. Use for past decisions, debugging notes, previous conversations, and project knowledge, especially when the context includes a MemSearch memory hint. Skip purely current-code questions or when the user asks to ignore memory.
readme_snippet: Steps Use memorysearch with a concrete query and topk: 5. It returns text containing a JSON array of objects with chunkhash, content and source. When calling through execute, return the search result and inspect its text before selecting hashes. Evaluate relevance before expanding results. Use memoryget with the most promising chunkhash values to read full Markdown sections. For claims requiring original dialogue, use memorytranscript with sessionid, turnid and dbpath from the expanded session: / turn: / db: anchor. Set context: 3; for an anchor without a turn, use limit: 10. If OpenCode transcript lookup fails after an upgrade, distinguish an incompatible host/plugin pair, an unavailable database or session/turn, and an incomplete V1-to-V2 database migration. See OpenCode diagnostics, also used by memory-config. Check the referenced conversation only; a lookup failure does not justify scanning unrelated transcripts. Keep existing markdown and session: / turn: / db: anchors unchanged.

description: Handle a data subject request (access, erasure, rectification, portability, objection) under GDPR Arts. 15-22. Use when the user receives or must answer such a request.
readme_snippet: Data subject request handling Identify which right is being invoked and verify the requester's identity proportionately. Deadline: one month from receipt, extendable by two months for complex or numerous requests (tell the requester within the first month). Check for valid grounds to refuse or limit (manifestly unfounded/excessive, third-party rights, legal retention duties, exemptions for erasure under Art. 17(3)). List the systems and processors to search; give a collection checklist. Draft the response letter: confirmation of processing, copy of data, and the Art. 15(1) information (purposes, recipients, retention, source, rights) for access requests. For refusals, state reasons and the right to complain. Log the request, dates and outcome.
